utility.notes: Portola Valley is a well-documented San Mateo County city within PG&E's core Northern California service territory.

value.name: WestLight Energy (formerly Peninsula Clean Energy)
value.notes: WestLight Energy's own site confirms it is San Mateo County's CCA, formed in 2015 after every city council in the county voted to establish it, serving the entire county (all cities/towns, including Portola Valley) since 2017. PG&E continues to deliver the power and provide billing/customer service.

permit_authority.value: Town of Portola Valley Planning & Building Department

interconnection_url.notes: PG&E's own utility-wide Net Energy Metering (NEM) program page.

value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized statewide budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025 and remains an active program per SGIP's own statewide announcements (most recently dated 2026-07-23). Administered across PG&E's entire distribution territory, which includes Portola Valley/San Mateo County.
value.eligibility: PG&E, SCE, or SDG&E residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Reused as a utility-level fact already established for other IOU-territory records this session: the CPUC-administered SGIP program applies uniformly across the named utility's entire distribution territory, directly verified via SGIP's own site (selfgenca.com) / the CPUC's own SGIP program page, including a program-status announcement as recent as 2026-07-23 confirming the program remains active.

value.name: Wet-signed and stamped building plan sets

required_documents.notes: This is the Town's general Building Permit submittal requirement (per its own Building Permit FAQs page, 'How do I apply for a building permit?'), not a solar-specific checklist; the Town confirms an approved checklist and standard plan process exists for expedited solar review, but the solar-specific document list itself was not directly fetched this session.

value.notes: The building department shall issue a building permit or other nondiscretionary permit within three business days of receipt of a complete application, including review by Woodside Fire Protection District, if the application meets the approved checklist and standard plan.

value.program_or_pathway: Expedited, streamlined solar permitting (Solar Rights Act / AB 2188 compliant)
other_conditions: Detached ADUs must provide conduit pathway infrastructure to support future solar installation (Solar Photovoltaic 'Ready' Infrastructure requirement)
Applications reviewed in coordination with Woodside Fire Protection District
